correctness.rationale: Exact disintegration: root attachments are independent Bernoulli with odds 1/(j-2). Elementary-symmetric log concavity proves nested inclusion couplings of cardinality-conditioned positive product measures. Shared independent nonroot parent variables convert the nested indicators to coordinatewise decreasing offspring counts. A positive-probability unique-parent event supplies strict expectation of leaf counts. Boundaries k=0 and k=n-2 are included. An exhaustive exact-rational checker verifies 2,579 assertions over 46,232 recursive trees of sizes 3..9; experiments are ancillary, not proofs.

originality.rationale: Searched the published mathematical records, known exact root-degree/leaf covariance result, and primary full-text root-coupling literature. Closest known exact covariance does not imply conditional coordinatewise stochastic ordering; Eslava--López--Ortiz use arbitrary coupling with conditioning in a degree window rather than a nesting for every exact root degree. Finite-state weighted-subset monotone coupling and consequence were not identified as previously formulated. This is a best-knowledge judgment, not a proof of priority.

The published covariance record was available as a searchable detailed summary rather than complete source package; its formula alone cannot imply the theorem.
Independent historical-priority verification has not been performed.

value.rationale: Joint root-degree and nonroot degree structure is a natural conditional question for recursive growth trees. The theorem supplies one coupling controlling every child-count coordinate simultaneously and all increasing set properties of leaf labels, not merely scalar covariance or expectation. It yields a full conditional multivariate order with strict leaf-mean inequalities at every degree, a structural property not supplied by available exact covariance literature. It has natural uses in comparing occupancy of children, leaf-set monotonicity, and conditional growth-profile inequalities. The standard weighted-subset lemma is deliberately not asserted to be independently novel.
